label: baseline

blocks.text: No.
The age of consent for HIVST has been reduced from 16 years to 12 years.

Anyone 12 years or older can give informed consent for medical care such as HIV testing services (HTS), PrEP, PEP, family planning, or medical male circumcision the 2012 Swaziland Child Welfare Act, but not for HIV treatment.

question: Which clients skip the HIVST screen and go straight to routine HIV testing with the national algorithm?
label: baseline

blocks.text: Clients who qualify for routine testing skip the HIVST screen.

These priority groups include malnourished and sick children, HIV-exposed children, clients with confirmed or presumptive TB disease, STI clients, index contacts, pregnant and lactating mothers, inpatients, and key populations (KPs).
All individuals 12 years and above are eligible for HIVST unless they qualify for routine testing.

Clients who qualify for routine testing skip the HIVST screen.

These priority groups include malnourished and sick children, HIV-exposed children, clients with confirmed or presumptive TB disease, STI clients, index contacts, pregnant and lactating mothers, inpatients, and key populations (KPs).

All individuals 12 years and above are eligible for HIVST unless they qualify for routine testing.

All individuals 12 years and above are eligible for HIVST unless they qualify for routine testing. If they test HIV negative, actively link them to prevention services. If the test results are HIV positive, offer partner notification services and link to treatment services.

label: baseline

blocks.text: No, do not use an HIV self-test to rule out HIV first.

question: Adult outpatient newly diagnosed with HIV, CD4 is 180. Should I send serum CrAg and urine TB-LAM?
label: baseline

blocks.text: Send urine TB-LAM because the patient has a CD4 count of 180 cells/ml, which is below 200 cells/ml.
Do not send serum CrAg screening for this patient because they have a CD4 count above 100 cells/ml but below 200 cells/ml.
TB LAM diagnosed patients are classified as bacteriologically confirmed TB patients. This means that if the TB LAM test is positive, the patient should be started on TB treatment.

Send urine TB-LAM because the patient has a CD4 count of 180 cells/ml, which is below 200 cells/ml.

Do not send serum CrAg screening for this patient because they have a CD4 count above 100 cells/ml but below 200 cells/ml.

TB LAM diagnosed patients are classified as bacteriologically confirmed TB patients. This means that if the TB LAM test is positive, the patient should be started on TB treatment.

raw_blocks.text: Yes, send serum CrAg and urine TB-LAM. For serum CrAg: start at a CD4 count ≤200 cells/ml. For urine TB-LAM: inpatients with CD4 ≤200 cell/ml, outpatients with CD4 ≤200 cell/ml.
For children under 10 years old, do not perform serum CrAg screening. For children under 10 years old, do urine TB-LAM if they are seriously ill or have symptoms of TB.
In adults and adolescents, perform urine TB-LAM for symptomatic patients regardless of CD4 count, and for inpatients and outpatients with CD4 ≤200 cells/ml.

question: Child living with HIV, 5 kg, starting first-line ART. Can I use the pALD (ABC/3TC/DTG 60/30/5 mg) dispersible tablet?
label: baseline

blocks.text: No, you cannot use the pALD dispersible tablet for a child living with HIV who weighs 5 kg.

question: Adult with AKI, potassium 6.8 mmol/L. What emergency treatment and doses?
label: baseline

blocks.text: Stabilize myocardium with bolus IV calcium gluconate 10% at 10 ml over 2 minutes (maximum 20 ml). DO NOT GIVE AT THE SAME TIME/SAME DRIP AS SODIUM BICARBONATE.

Shift potassium with ONLY 5 units (five units) short acting insulin (Actrapid) in 50 ml of dextrose 50% over 30 minutes (higher insulin amounts can accumulate in kidney failure and cause dangerous hypoglycaemia).
Shift with salbutamol nebulizer at 10-20 mg every 1-2 hours (MONITOR FOR TACHYCARDIA AND ARRHYTHMIAS).

question: What are the tracing steps for a client on ART who is more than 28 days late and can't be reached by phone?
label: baseline

blocks.text: For a client on ART who is more than 28 days late and can't be reached by phone, follow up with community follow-up.

Community follow-up commences at defaulter stage; in-person community follow-up is conducted at community level; attempts depend on follow-up and are escalated the need of the client using the escalation plan.

The client may be followed multiple times depending on follow-up outcome; frequency of follow-up may be reduced until a conclusive outcome is achieved; file may be closed after a home visit in resource-limited settings or if a conclusive outcome is attained and the escalation plan exhausted.

question: Woman living with HIV on an efavirenz-based regimen wants hormonal contraception. Which methods are least affected by her ART?
label: baseline

blocks.text: Women living with asymptomatic or mild HIV clinical disease (WHO stage 1 or 2) can generally use the following hormonal contraceptive methods without restriction: COCs, CICs, combined contraceptive patches and rings, POPs, POIs (DMPA and NET-EN), and LNG and ETG implants.
The efficacy of the Levonorgestrel releasing IUD is unlikely to be affected by ART.
There are no known interactions between Dapivirine and contraceptive hormones.

message:
Women living with asymptomatic or mild HIV clinical disease (WHO stage 1 or 2) can generally use the following hormonal contraceptive methods without restriction: COCs, CICs, combined contraceptive patches and rings, POPs, POIs (DMPA and NET-EN), and LNG and ETG implants.

The efficacy of the Levonorgestrel releasing IUD is unlikely to be affected by ART.

There are no known interactions between Dapivirine and contraceptive hormones.

Sources: [4] fp-2021, 14.1 Appendix 1: Summary of Recommendation - Medical Eligibility Criteria, PDF page 96; [11] fp-2021, 14.6 Appendix 6: Effect of Specific Arvs on the Effectiveness of Hormonal Contraceptive Methods, PDF page 116; [15] prep-2025, PrEP Ring and Other Drug Interactions, PDF page 19

Progestin levels with POPs do not appear to be reduced by some PIs, but no efficacy data are available.
Levels of DMPA do not appear to be reduced by ARVs (including efavirenz), studies on Net-En when used with ART are not available.
Limited evidence suggests that efficacy of the Levonorgestrel releasing IUD is unlikely to be affected by ART.

To start daily oral PrEP, take a loading dose of two tablets at PrEP initiation and delay sex for at least two hours, ideally closer to 24 hours, at which time drug levels will be maximally effective to prevent HIV acquisition from sexual exposures. For injection-related exposures, you will need to take one tablet daily for seven days prior to exposure for drug levels to be maximally effective.
